title: JSON Lines
statement: Implement `solve(lines)`. Each non-blank line is a JSON value. Skip blank lines. Collect successful values in `values` and the 1-based line numbers of failures in `errors`. A line number counts every line, including blanks. Return `{"values": [...], "errors": [...]}`. Do not use eval.
constraints: Blank lines are skipped and are not errors
hints: json.loads each non-blank line inside a try.
Append the value or the line number. A blank line does neither.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: JSON Lines is one JSON value per line.

editorial: JSON Lines is one JSON value per line. One bad line should not throw away the file. Recording the line number lets a caller fix the file. eval is the wrong parser because a line can be hostile text, and json.loads will not execute it.
